questions.stem: According to the lecture, the medical history reveals approximately what share of the information needed for an accurate diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The history reveals 60–80% of the information needed; the studies shown give history 60–76%, examination 12–20%, tests 11–20%. A: Roughly the share from examination or tests. B, C: Too low. E: Too high; examination and tests still add information.

questions.stem: In Beckman's 1984 study, how long did patients usually need to finish their opening statement if not interrupted?
questions.explanation: Most patients who weren't interrupted finished in under 60 seconds and none took longer than 150 seconds, so interrupting saves little time and costs information. A: 18 seconds is when doctors interrupted. C: Longer than most needed. D: 150 seconds was the maximum, not the usual. E: No patient took this long.

questions.stem: A doctor types on the computer while asking questions. The patient pauses before answering and shifts in her chair to catch the doctor's attention. Which non-verbal element is missing?
questions.explanation: Without eye contact, patients give less information, withhold their initial reply until eye contact is given, and use body movement to catch the doctor's gaze. A: Handshake or physical contact. B: Physical distance between communicators. C: Rate, volume, rhythm, intonation. D: Punctuality, being hurried or slow to respond.

questions.stem: Which is an appropriate way to open the interview after introductions?

options.C: "What would you like to discuss today?"

questions.explanation: An open question identifies the patient's reasons for coming. A: Leading. B, D: Closed questions too early. E: Doctor's agenda first.

questions.stem: Which property belongs to non-verbal rather than verbal communication?

options.A: It is discrete, with clear endpoints
options.B: It occurs in a single mode at a time
options.C: It is mostly under voluntary control
options.D: It continues as long as both are present
options.E: It carries less weight than verbal cues

questions.explanation: Non-verbal communication is continuous, occurs in several modes at once, and operates at or beyond conscious awareness. A, B, C: Properties of verbal communication. E: Non-verbal wins out over verbal cues.

questions.stem: Diagnostic errors occur in 10–15% of diagnoses. According to the lecture, about 80% of these errors stem from:
questions.explanation: 80% of diagnostic errors are based on information missed in the history or physical examination. A, B: Tests contribute only a minority of diagnostic information. D, E: Not cited as the source of diagnostic error.
